subject: Deal-mapped pool dimensioning: traffic profiles + surge policy
messages:
From: Michael Yang <michael@datafold.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot + Dedicated ask for Evr integration

Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Evr is ready to move from pilot to a pilot+first production tenant for a small set of customers. Their traffic profile is bursty (hourly spikes driven by batch jobs) and they need a predictable committed pool with burst/overflow into hosted.

High-level asks:
- Start with a small dedicated pool for US region for 2 GPUs (A100 equivalent), with ability to burst to hosted when 95th-percentile bursts hit.
- EU presence is nice-to-have for latency-sensitive customers (1 GPU to start).
- APAC not required immediately but must be supported in roadmap.

Can you send a proposed sizing + surge policy that maps to the deal milestones? Attached is our internal SLA draft.

Thanks,
Michael
CTO, DataFold

Attachments: evr_sla_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Michael Yang <michael@datafold.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot + Dedicated ask for Evr integration

Thanks Michael — looping in Sales Ops and Capacity.

High level ask from my side: produce a deal-mapped pool dimensioning that shows baseline committed GPUs, expected token/sec and 95th-percentile burst headroom, and clear overflow paths (hosted tier, regional fallback). I'd like one slide per region with a recommended rollout schedule tied to the contract milestones in HubSpot (deal closes -> 30d -> 90d).

Marissa — can you start with a rough matrix for US/EU/APAC by EOD Friday? Include gross estimates and assumptions (concurrency, avg seq length, caching hit-rate) so we can validate with Engineering.

Karthik — procurement lead: flag any multi-region SKU constraints or minimum commit terms that would affect pricing/lead time.

Jonas — engineering constraints, especially KV-cache warmup time for bursty batch traffic; if we need warm pools in each region we should call that out.

CC: Vivek to advise on account exec readiness and any regional compliance asks.

Irene
Head of Sales Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: q4_deal_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Michael Yang <michael@datafold.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot + Dedicated ask for Evr integration — initial sizing matrix

Attaching the draft matrix and a short summary below. Numbers are conservative and include a 25% safety factor for traffic variance. See attached CSV for per-endpoint token/sec samples.

Summary (baseline committed pools):
- US (primary): 2 x A100 equiv (committed); expected baseline throughput 350k tokens/min, 95th-percentile bursts up to 1.1M tokens/min. Suggest surge policy: burst to hosted + one-time regional buffer of 2 ephemeral GPUs for 2 weeks post-launch.
- EU: 1 x A100 equiv (committed); baseline 80k tokens/min, bursts to 250k tokens/min. Overflow to hosted EU region.
- APAC: zero committed to start; recommend pre-warm option (cold standby) if customer signs APAC SLAs within 60d.

Assumptions included in CSV: avg seq length=480 tokens, concurrency=45, cache hit-rate=12% (prefix reuse), steady hourly batch windows at 02:00 & 14:00 PST.

Next steps: procurement constraints and cost estimates from Karthik; engineering validation on warmup and autoscaler timelines from Jonas. If we can compress rollout to 30d for US, we propose a 2-week canary then open for broader customer traffic.

Marissa
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: traffic_profile_samples.csv, surge_policy_draft.md

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 09:33:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot + Dedicated ask for Evr integration — procurement notes

Quick procurement note: committed pool SKUs require a 3-month minimum on our cloud resale agreements for A100-equivalent units in EU and APAC in the provider contracts we maintain. US has more flexible monthly commits. For the deal economics: if Evr is willing to sign a 6-month reservation on EU (1 GPU) we can pass through a 12% discount — otherwise price will be ~18% higher due to short-term provisioning.

Also callout: lead time for APAC region pre-warm nodes is ~4 weeks for HSM/KMS onboarding and networking (if customer wants private VPC config). If Evr accepts hosted fallback only (no VPC), we can get region visibility in 10 days.

I'll add a line item cost breakdown to the HubSpot deal and flag the procurement acceptance checkbox.

Karthik
Head of Procurement Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Michael Yang <michael@datafold.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Pilot + Dedicated ask for Evr integration — engineering validation + action items

Thanks all — validated Marissa's baseline using simulator runs. A few engineering notes and an action list: 

Engineering notes:
- KV-cache warmup: cold start for a 2 GPU pool targeting their workload will see ~90s median warmup for typical conversational prefixes; for the batch spikes we should consider keeping a small warm pool persistent during the first 30 days.
- Burst handling: implement a surge policy that allows burst routing to hosted with token throttling at 1.2x baseline to avoid queue collapse.
- Observability: add two new dashboard panels (per-route token/sec and 95th latency) for deal tracking.

Action items:
- Marissa: finalize the matrix and upload to the HubSpot deal record (done).
- Karthik: confirm cost pass-through numbers and add procurement checkbox in the contract.
- Irene/Vivek: align on sales cadence; target close date 2026-12-20 and a US canary 30d post-close.

Michael — we can start provisioning dev prewarmed pool tomorrow if you sign the PO; otherwise we'll default to hosted fallback for bursts.

Jonas
Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
